subject: research/selfrep-dpgrid
professional: a numerical analyst / optimal-control researcher (dynamic programming, semi-Lagrangian schemes) who would referee a grid-convergence study for a journal or workshop

evidence.correctness: Ran `python3 experiments/run.py`-equivalent numbers through an independent vectorised numpy re-implementation (scratchpad ind.py, written without reading run.py's loop, using the satmarket Euler model). Recomputed: (1) exact all-copy value 50*(1.02)^600 = 7228914.056 vs reported J_bb 7228914.1 (c=1e4/1e3, s=50) and linear-market 'exact' value; (2) best bang-bang for c=1e3,s=12.5 by own 601-switch scan = 1807228.51 at ts=600 vs reported 1807228.5; (3) index-rule DP table c=1e4,s=50 at 100/400/800 points = 5795760.14 / 6623288.50 / 6937383.78 vs reported 5795760.1 / 6623288.5 / 6937383.8; (4) n-rule at 100/400/800 = 4422034.19 / 6406992.21 / 6874950.81 vs reported 4422034.2 / 6406992.2 / 6874950.8; (5) c=1e3,s=12.5 index 400 = 1647581.51 and c=1e3,s=50 index 1600 = 7014777.11, both match. Every number matches to the digit. Caveat: my DP uses the same algorithm, so it checks implementation and transcription, not the claim that the table converges to the true continuous optimum. The only source-independent anchor is the all-copy closed form. Policy values J were not independently recomputed (only table values); results.txt gap and ratio arithmetic spot-checked (c=1e3,s=50: 800->1600 J change 0.26%, README headline says 'about 0.15%', see claims).
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: 100..1600 point refinement, two interpolation rules, 81-level run, three cases, Richardson extrapolation, linear-market check, `python3 -m unittest` (4 tests) and experiments/run.py all exist and results.txt contains every quoted row. experiments/figure.py and gap.svg exist but are not mentioned in the README. Project is registered in research/_homepage/projects.json. Not done, and honestly listed in Limitations: diagnosis of the bias, step refinement, cash constraint. The stated question (is the table converged) is answered for the table and policy. I did not load the live page.
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 4 tests, OK, 0.06 s. Three seeded mutations in src/selfrep_dpgrid/model.py, each reverted (git status clean): (a) n-rule target scaled by 1.01: 2 tests failed (caught); (b) swapped interpolation weights f and 1-f in the successor value: 3 tests failed (caught); (c) `val > best` -> `val >= best` (tie-break): all pass (equivalent-ish, not a real miss). Weakness: the tests are loose (2% and 3% tolerances, tiny T=20-40 h problems) and none pins any number in results.txt or the README headline (policy within 0.3% of converged, table 2-3% low at 1600), so a bug that shifts the 600 h results by 1% would pass. The terminal-value test only asserts >= s, not equality. No test of the linear-market all-copy closed form that run.py itself prints.
evidence.craft: Read src/selfrep_dpgrid/model.py (61 lines), tests/test_dpgrid.py, experiments/run.py, and sibling selfrep-terminalmarket model.py. dp_solve is a near-verbatim copy of terminalmarket's dp_solve (the README calls it 're-implemented with a second interpolation option'), so a fix to one engine will not reach the other. sys.path.insert hacks to three sibling trees; run.py has no `if __name__` guard and runs 40 s on import; no input validation (n_points=1 divides by zero, u_levels=1 likewise, a negative s breaks `best=-1.0` initial value). The successor table is precomputed per (i,j), a good touch. Stdlib only, 4 s per 1600-point solve in pure Python. Readable and small; not above reviewer-acceptable bar given the copied engine and silent assumptions.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt: 'J changes by at most about 0.3% from 800 to 1600' true (0.26% worst); but the bold headline 'converged to about 0.15%' is the best case, not the worst (0.26%). 'table below J by 8-13% at 400, 4-6% at 800, 2-3% at 1600' true. 'index rule above all-copy +18.7%/+0.21%, n rule -20.4%/-0.15%' true. 'DP policy ties best switch within 0.2%' true, but undisclosed: in all three cases the best bang-bang switch is ts=600, i.e. never stop copying (J_bb identical 7228914.1 for both s=50 cases, equal to the all-copy closed form), so 'bang-bang is not beaten' means 'the DP policy is all-copy', a degenerate regime; the sibling research/selfrep-exactdp (whose homepage summary cites this project) finds 4.7-7.1% gains over the best switch in other (s, c) regimes that this study never visits. The 'so the earlier table gap was discretisation' conclusion is stated while the Limitations say the cause is undiagnosed. Richardson values of 100.15-100.76% of J_bb are read as 'within 1% of optimum' though they exceed 100% and rest on an unverified first-order assumption. Module docstring says the index rule 'overstates a convex function of log n', yet the table sits below J. Disclaimers (all inputs assumed, simulated only) are present and honest; hedging is good.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can reuse the idea (compare table value with simulated policy value, vary grid and interpolation) but not the result: the cases are the all-copy corner, the bias is undiagnosed, no comparison to the Pontryagin/singular-arc solution that selfrep-singulararc already derives, no error bound, and the n-rule hypothesis (exact for linear terminal reward) failed without explanation. Nearest prior work: semi-Lagrangian DP convergence for HJB equations (Falcone and Ferretti, Semi-Lagrangian Approximation Schemes for Linear and HJB Equations, SIAM 2013; Bellman 1957) establishes first-order convergence under these conditions and standard interpolation/higher-order remedies, so the finding that a 1-D log-grid table converges slowly and linearly is known, not new. In-repo, selfrep-exactdp (grid-aligned controls, table equals policy to 1e-14) supersedes this study's open question. Novelty: low; value is as an internal sanity check of the earlier project, not a publishable result. Against research/CLAUDE.md's PhD+ programme bar: 61 lines of model, assumed inputs (W from selfrep-growth only), no programme entry in PROGRAMMES.md, no deep-tech application.
evidence.domain: A numerical analyst would first ask for: an observed convergence order (the README infers 'roughly halving per doubling' from five grids but fits no order and gives no log-log slope), a convergence test of the control discretisation jointly with the state grid, a reference solution (the continuous-time optimum or Pontryagin singular arc exists in-repo and was not used), and a higher-order or monotone-scheme comparison. A Richardson extrapolation from two grids that produces values above the policy value is a flag the study notes but does not resolve. Euler step is fixed at 1 h (k dt = 0.02), the same order as the effects measured. Stated limits are honest. Practice departed from: standard verification of DP codes against a closed-form or manufactured solution beyond the single all-copy case.

defects.what: In every reported case the best bang-bang switch is ts=600 (never switch; J_bb equals the all-copy closed form), so 'DP policy ties bang-bang' is a degenerate result that the README does not disclose; regimes where the DP beats a switch (selfrep-exactdp) are not examined
Headline 'policy value converged to about 0.15%' is the best case; worst case in results.txt is 0.26% (c=1e3, s=50, 800 to 1600 points); convergence is asserted from 800 vs 1600 only, no order fitted
Tests are loose (2%, 3% tolerances, T=20-40 h) and pin no number from results.txt; a tie-break change passes and a 1% shift in 600 h results would not be caught
dp_solve is a near-verbatim copy of selfrep-terminalmarket's engine instead of an optional interpolation argument there; no input validation (n_points=1, u_levels=1 divide by zero)

Docstring claims the index rule overstates a convex function of log n, contradicted by the table lying 2-13% below J in the main cases; Richardson values above 100% of J_bb are not resolved; figure.py and gap.svg not in README

verdict: Numbers are right and reproducible: five independent recomputations (all-copy closed form, best switch, DP tables for both interpolation rules at several grid sizes) matched results.txt to the digit, the 4 tests pass and two of three seeded mutations were caught, and the limits are stated honestly. It does not meet the bar: claims is 2 (the 0.15% headline is the best case, and the 'bang-bang is not beaten' result is the degenerate never-switch corner, undisclosed) and verification is 2 (loose tests that pin no reported number). As research it is a small sanity check of an earlier project, not a new or publishable result: first-order convergence of semi-Lagrangian DP is known, the bias is undiagnosed, the in-repo Pontryagin solution is not used as reference, and the sibling selfrep-exactdp already supersedes it. Finished (completeness 3) but not at the PhD+ bar of research/CLAUDE.md.
